Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodai.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Jan 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC trial planning / workload intake - HealthTech Labs

Hi Aaron / Emma —

Great to speak today — thanks for walking us through your evaluation goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the trial: 

Summary of what we heard (please correct if I got anything wrong):
- Success criteria: 95% of inference calls must be < 200ms p50 and < 400ms p95; classification accuracy on your labeled eval set >= 88%; no PII leakage in outputs.
- Evaluation plan: 4-week POC — week 0 provisioning & dataset ingestion, week 1 baseline run, week 2 tuning & quantization tests, week 3 regression checks & final evaluation.
- Ownership: Marissa will run the eval plan and reporting; Dylan will handle infra sizing and deployment; I will coordinate logistics and commercial questions.
- Timeline: target start week of 2027-02-07, with final evaluation complete by 2027-03-06.

Workload intake items we need from you to size the POC accurately (attached is a quick template):
1) Typical RPS (avg) and peak RPS / burst patterns:
2) Average input token length and average output token length (or 95th percentile)
3) Concurrency and number of simultaneous users during peaks
4) Sample payloads (sanitized) and any long-tail/edge cases
5) Data residency / compliance constraints

Can you fill the attached template and share the CSV export of a representative week? If you prefer, paste the numbers directly in a reply. I've attached a success-criteria template and example workload CSV to make this quick.

Next steps (proposed):
- Aaron: confirm the workload numbers and timeline by Monday 2027-02-01
- Marissa: we'll send a formal MUTUAL ACTION PLAN after we get the workload data
- Dylan: pre-size infra and propose a recommended model / quantization profile

Thanks — excited to run this with you.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodai.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments:
- poc-success-criteria-template.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- healthtech-workload-template.csv (CSV template)
From: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@healthtechlabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Emma Gonzalez <emma@healthtechlabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodai.com>
Date: Sun, 31 Jan 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC trial planning / workload intake - HealthTech Labs

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear recap. Confirming high-level details and sharing the initial workload numbers below (we also attached a one-week export):

Workload snapshot (representative week):
- Avg RPS: 12 requests/sec (steady-state business hours)
- Typical peak: short bursts up to ~200 requests/min for 5–10 minute windows during report generation (we see these 3–4x per day)
- Concurrency: typical concurrency 8 concurrent inference workers; peak concurrency ~60 during bursts
- Input token length: avg 110 tokens, 95th percentile 420 tokens (we have some long-form notes)
- Output token length: avg 45 tokens, 95th percentile 180 tokens
- Typical payload size (sanitized): ~8KB for long-form notes (JSON)

Compliance / data residency: We need EU data to remain in EU region for any EU-based patient data, but this POC will be only US datasets so we're fine for now. For production we'll require SOC 2 + data residency controls.

Timeline: The week of 2027-02-07 works for us to start the POC. We'll aim to have the cleaned sample payloads to you by 2027-02-03.

Questions:
1) For the burst patterns (200 req/min), can you recommend a sizing approach for autoscaling during the POC?
2) Can we run with a quantized model for cost reasons, and still meet the latency SLOs?

Attaching: healthtech-workload-export.csv (sanitized)

Thanks — Aaron
Dir. Product Operations | HealthTech Labs
aaron.lee@healthtechlabs.com | +1 (646) 555-0189
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
To: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@healthtechlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodai.com>
Date: Sun, 31 Jan 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC trial planning / workload intake - HealthTech Labs

Perfect — thanks for the numbers, Aaron. Helpful and aligns with what we expected. Quick answers and next steps: 

- Autoscaling approach for bursts: Dylan and I talked through two options — pre-warm a small burst capacity (reserved instances to cover ~150 req/min) plus autoscale policy to handle the very short spikes; for the POC we recommend a mix of reserved + burst to avoid cold-starts and to keep costs predictable. Dylan, I'll defer to you for the exact sizing.
- Quantized models: yes — we can run int8/4-bit quantized variants for the experiment. We'll run a baseline float model in week 1 to collect latency/quality metrics then run quantization experiments in week 2 and compare. If quality drops below your success threshold we'll revert or try hybrid quantization.

Ownership & deliverables: 
- Marissa: will lead the evaluation reporting and will request the labeled eval set (target delivery 2027-02-04).
- Dylan: please propose the infra config (instance types, reserved burst capacity, autoscale policy) by EOD 2027-02-01.
- Ben: will create the mutual action plan and DocuSign for the POC statement of work.

I’ll mark the HubSpot deal with the POC milestone and share the mutual action plan once Marissa confirms the evaluation dataset arrival.

Cheers,
Ben

Thanks — quick infra sizing note based on Aaron's numbers: 

Preliminary infra plan (POC):
- Model: recommend using the rwd-medium family (good mix of latency/quality) for baseline; run int8 quantized rwd-medium-q for week 2 experiments.
- Instance sizing: 2 x A100-80GB equiv nodes for baseline throughput; add 1-2 smaller GPU nodes to cover burst capacity (use warm standby containers).
- Autoscale: policy to add nodes when queue latency > 100ms for > 30s, with a max scale to cover ~250 req/min. Warm standby + reserved burst should handle the 5–10 minute spikes without cold starts.
- Expected inference p50: ~160–200ms baseline (float); quantized p50 expected ~120–150ms. We'll validate with the week 1 run.

Action items for Aaron / HealthTech: please provide 3–5 sanitized sample payloads (representative long, medium, short) and a small labeled eval set to help validate accuracy. If you can attach them to this thread or upload to the Drive link Ben shared that'll speed things up.

I’ve attached a short sizing note (inference-sizing-notes.md) with assumptions and cost ballpark. I’ll finalize node counts once I’ve run the first baseline.

—Dylan
SRE, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwoodai.com
